sections.html:
Directly across the Pearl River from Jackson, on its east bank, Pearl is Rankin County's largest city. In 2020 it had 27,115 residents in 10,926 households, with a median age of 36.1 years. The city covers about 25.6 square miles and borders Flowood, Brandon, Richland and Jackson. U.S. Highway 80 is the main commercial street, and Interstate 20, Interstate 55, U.S. 49 and Mississippi Highway 25 (Lakeland Drive) all serve the area.

The city runs its own city hall, police, fire department and school district, though plenty of people lump it in with greater Jackson. Permits, code questions and school boundaries run through the city, while the property tax bill comes from Rankin County.

Citywide, median household income is $61,695 and median property value is $182,500. Such averages blur a lot: a three-bedroom ranch near Old Brandon Road and a house with deferred repairs will land far apart. Much of the housing came with suburban growth out of Jackson in the 1960s, which means sellers often own houses whose roofs, foundations and systems have aged. When a problem makes a house hard to finance, a cash buyer who takes the property as is becomes a practical option.

The county values each parcel and sends the bill. Payment is due February 1 and covers the assessment year before, and a February 1 that falls on a weekend or holiday simply moves to the next Monday with no penalty or interest.

The constitution sorts houses into classes. A single-family home its owner lives in is Class I, assessed at 10 percent of true value. A rental, or an inherited house nobody occupies, is Class II at 15 percent. The bill comes from true value times that ratio times the combined county, city and school district millage. Real property must be revalued at least every four years.

Bills are mailed by December. The Tax Collector's number is (601) 825-1467, and the county also has an online payment page. A parcel that stays unpaid is sold in August, though the owner keeps two years from that date to redeem before it matures to the buyer or the State. Anyone behind on taxes must clear them before a clean title can pass, so request a payoff figure early.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and a Pearl sale
sections.html:
Who lives in the house on January 1 is who can claim the exemption, so a sale changes the claimant. To qualify, a buyer has to own the home and occupy it as a primary residence that day, with the deed on file at the Chancery Clerk before January 7. Filing happens at the county Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1.

Homestead tierWho qualifiesBenefit
RegularOwners younger than 65Credit of up to $300
Age or disabilityOwners 65 or older, or totally disabledExempt on the first $7,500 of assessed value
Disabled service membersSome disabled former service members and surviving spousesFull exemption

Closing in spring most likely means missing that year's exemption, and a landlord never qualifies. The seller's exemption does not carry over, so the next owner may need a new application. Raise it at the closing table so the next tax bill holds no surprise.

sections.h2: What a Pearl seller must disclose
sections.html:
Most sellers must give the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement under Section 89-1-503, as soon as practicable before title moves. The contract or an addendum notes that it was done.

With an offer already on the table, a late statement lets the buyer cancel in writing: three days after hand delivery or five after mailing. Blank or partly filled answers leave the buyer presumed to be on notice to ask, and agents are not disciplined for the omission.

  • Be straight about roof leaks, foundation movement and earlier water damage.
  • Repair receipts settle most buyer questions, so keep them.
  • Give the statement out with the first offer, so no one gets a cancellation window.

Even an as-is cash buyer receives the disclosure, then simply prices in repairs rather than asking you to make them.

sections.h2: Ways to sell fast in Pearl
sections.html:
Hire an agent, sell straight to an investor for cash, or repair first and list afterward: those are the Pearl options, and house condition plus your closing deadline decide among them.

  • A listing is best for a house in good shape, if you can sit through showings, inspections and the wait for loan approval.
  • Cash fits houses with repair needs, tax or probate pressure, tenants, or a move set by a deadline.
  • Repairing first can pay if the work is cosmetic and cheap, but costs climb and finishing takes time.

New employers and road links may help neighborhood demand over time, but they do not fix a house that needs work today. Do not count on future projects to carry a listing.

sections.h2: What buyers will want to see
sections.html: A Pearl buyer will probably raise the roof, foundation, drainage and old water damage, and will compare your price with other houses in the neighborhood rather than the citywide median. Have repair receipts, permit sign-offs and your latest tax bill in one folder. An older suburban house with a documented history is easier to price, and it gives a cash buyer less room to discount for unknowns.

Some Pearl news can help a listing talk. West Rankin Industrial Park is the city's main industrial area, and Siemens Energy announced a grid-component plant there in 2026, with an investment of up to $300 million and up to 300 jobs. The West Rankin Parkway opened in November 2025 and links Highway 80 in Pearl to Flowood Drive in Flowood. Outlets of Mississippi, a 315,000 square foot outlet center, adds to the shopping base, and Pearl has been a Mississippi Main Street community since 2021. Mention what is near your street, but let the house itself carry the price.

On closing day, the signature that matters most is yours on the deed, notarized, so bring photo identification. Your title company or attorney will have prepared the payoff of any mortgage and the split of the year's tax bill. Ask to see the settlement statement a day ahead and check that each line matches what you agreed to. After you sign, the deed goes to the Rankin County Chancery Clerk to be recorded.

Every sale should begin with a title search, which reveals liens, unpaid taxes and whether the seller really holds legal title. The Rankin County Chancery Clerk wants a notarized seller signature on the deed, a legal description with indexing instructions, and contact details for sellers, buyers and whoever prepared it. An attorney or title company searches the records and drafts the deed. For permit work left open, ask the City of Pearl's Community Development office on Old Brandon Road.

Cash Home Buyers works with Pearl sellers who want a straightforward as-is sale, and we explain what we can and cannot offer up front.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell my house in Pearl, MS?
faqs.a: That depends on the route you pick. Cash can close once title work is done. A listing also has to get through showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal. Title problems and unpaid taxes slow both.

faqs.q: Do I need to make repairs before selling in Pearl?
faqs.a: No. The state sets no repair requirement for a sale. You do still owe the buyer a completed written property condition disclosure statement, and as-is buyers usually price repairs into their offer.

faqs.q: When are Rankin County property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1 is the deadline for the prior assessment year. When it lands on a weekend or holiday, paying the next Monday costs nothing extra.
Pearl runs its own district, the Pearl Public School District, with schools from lower elementary through Pearl High School.

faqs.q: Who records the deed when a Pearl house sells?
faqs.a: The Rankin County Chancery Clerk files it. A title company or attorney usually prepares the deed, which must carry a notarized seller signature and a legal description.
